title: AZ-800: Administering Windows Server Hybrid Core Infrastructure
description: Prepares for Microsoft's exam AZ-800 (the first of the two exams for Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Associate): Active Directory Domain Services on premises and in Azure, Group Policy, hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra Connect, managing Windows Server with Windows Admin Center, Azure Arc and PowerShell, Hyper-V and Windows Server containers, DNS, DHCP and hybrid networking, and file servers, Storage Spaces, DFS and Azure File Sync. Practised on a simulated Windows Server network with a PowerShell console on every server and simple practice consoles.
disclaimer: Cert Lab is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Microsoft. Microsoft, Windows Server, Active Directory, Hyper-V, Azure, Azure Arc, Microsoft Entra and Windows Admin Center are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. This course follows Microsoft's public "skills measured" outline for exam AZ-800 as Cert Lab understood it in 2026 (five areas: Deploy and manage AD DS in on-premises and cloud environments, about 30-35%; Manage Windows Servers and workloads in a hybrid environment, about 10-15%; Manage virtual machines and containers, about 15-20%; Implement and manage an on-premises and hybrid networking infrastructure, about 15-20%; Manage storage and file services, about 15-20%). The weights are approximate and Microsoft changes the outline from time to time: check the current study guide on Microsoft Learn before you book the exam. AZ-801 (configuring advanced services) is a separate exam and not part of this course. Every lesson, question and lab was written for Cert Lab; none comes from Microsoft's exams or training. The servers, the practice consoles and the Azure side are a simulation written by Cert Lab: they behave like Windows Server 2022 and Azure for what the course covers, but nothing signs in anywhere and nothing reaches a real service or this PC.
examNote: A Cert Lab practice exam in the style of Microsoft's: single and multiple answer questions, drag-and-order questions, Yes / No statement series, a case study (a scenario with several questions), and a few hands-on tasks on the practice servers and consoles. Scores are shown from 1 to 1000 with 700 to pass, like Microsoft's reports; Microsoft doesn't publish how its scores are calculated, so this is only an approximation (each item's points as a share of the total). Results are shown per objective, and the review explains every answer. Some names and numbers change from one attempt to the next.
examHint: Hands-on tasks are done in the practice area on the right: a PowerShell console on each server (pick the server), or the practice consoles (Users and Computers, Group Policy, DNS, Windows Admin Center, Azure). You are CORP\Administrator everywhere. Changes replicate between the domain controllers on the simulated clock: use Skip time when a task depends on it. Questions: pick the answer or answers asked for; for a drag-and-order question, move the right actions into the answer list in the right order.
aboutMachines:
The practice network belongs to Harborline Logistics (made up): the Active Directory domain corp.example (NetBIOS name CORP) with two domain controllers, DC1 (10.10.0.10, head office) and DC2 (10.20.0.11, at the branch office but still in the HQ site at the start), the file server FS1, the Hyper-V host HV1 (with three virtual machines and a Docker engine), CORE1 (Server Core), the member server SRV1 (DHCP, Windows Admin Center) and the Windows 11 client CL1. The partner company Tidewater Freight has its own forest, tidewater.example (DNS server 192.168.50.10). The Azure side is a pretend subscription (Harborline Production) with a virtual network, two Azure VMs, Azure Arc, Microsoft Entra Connect and Azure File Sync; the Microsoft Entra tenant is harborline.onmicrosoft.example with the verified domain harborline.example.

Every machine has the simulated Windows PowerShell 5.1 console with the modules it would have (ActiveDirectory and GroupPolicy on the DCs and SRV1, DnsServer on the DCs, DhcpServer on SRV1, Hyper-V on HV1...). The practice consoles are Cert Lab's own drawings, not Microsoft's: they follow Active Directory Users and Computers, Group Policy Management, DNS Manager, Windows Admin Center and the Azure portal closely enough to practise the clicks. Replication, Group Policy refresh (90 minutes on members, 5 on DCs), DHCP leases and sync cycles run on a simulated clock: Skip time moves it on.
